items.title: The design depends on an unanswered data-access request
items.whyItMatters: A register-based follow-up and a school survey need different approvals, staff time and analysis.
items.opportunity: Prepare both branches so either can start as soon as access is decided.

items.title: Register misses doses given outside schools
items.whyItMatters: Register coverage ran 4 to 9 points low where community doses were common (claim c1).
items.opportunity: Apply a correction or validate a sample of records against cards.

items.title: Deprivation and home language are entangled
items.whyItMatters: Both lower coverage and consent return, and they cannot yet be separated (claims c3, c4).
items.opportunity: Record school-level language data and report both stratifiers.

items.title: Why consent forms did not return is unknown
items.whyItMatters: Unreturned forms explain more of the gap than refusals.
items.opportunity: Count forms sent, returned and refused by school and delivery route.

errorsFound: District totals mask school-level gaps; a single coverage figure would hide where next year's effort should go.
reevaluation: Both branches share the outcome and stratifiers; only the data source, sampling and approvals differ.
summary: Four gaps: undecided data access, register undercount, entangled equity axes, and unexplained consent return.
